Maya Singh: Heads-up 1: postmortem for yesterday's model-registry auth cascade is linked here: https://rwd.co/pm/2630-auth-cascade. Root cause: upstream provider started rate-limiting token issuance under a maintenance window, causing short token storms and client-side retries to amplify failures. The PM calls for 4 follow-ups: (A) token pooling/proxy, (B) short-term TTL increase for cached tokens, (C) synthetic token check + SLA ticket, (D) runbook + telemetry tweaks. Need owners + realistic ETAs so we can publish the remediation plan by tomorrow morning.

Ethan Zhou: I'll own (A) token pooling/proxy. Idea: lightweight token-broker service in front of provider that accepts pooled requests and throttles outgoing to provider. Implementation: prototype in go, integrate with existing auth SDK via env var AUTH_BROKER_URL. Risks: added service, HA concerns. ETA: prototype by 2026-03-29, staging test 2026-04-03, canary 2026-04-10.

Priya Menon: I can take (B) TTL tweak + prefetch. Plan: increase cached token TTL from 10s -> 45s and add a prefetch hook before expiry. Will add feature-flag and a safety cap to avoid stale tokens. ETA: PR 2026-03-26, rollout 2026-03-31. Low-risk but needs careful QA for token validity windows.

Diego Alvarez: I'll do (C) synthetic checks and SLA kickoff. I'll create a synthetic that hits token endpoint every 20s from 3 regions and hook to ops pager. Also opening procurement ticket to push vendor for rate-limit reconciliation and response RTO improvements. ETA: synthetic + alerts 2026-03-25, SLA ticket 2026-03-27.

Ruth Baxter: I'll update runbooks (D) and add a section for "model-registry degraded read-only fallback" - steps to switch to read-only and notify teams. Also adding a checklist for when to flip AUTH_BROKER feature-flag. ETA: draft runbook 2026-03-24, final 2026-03-29.

Maya Singh: Thanks team. Couple of cross-cutting questions: 1) do we want to pursue the token-broker long-term or treat it as temporary until vendor SLA is improved? 2) can we standardize client-side jittered exponential backoff as default in the SDK?

Ethan Zhou: Token-broker is probably medium-term; it buys resilience at cost of another moving part. If vendor agrees to SLA changes within 30 days, we could deprecate broker. Let's treat it as reversible infra.

Priya Menon: I'll standardize backoff in the SDK. I'll push a change that makes jittered backoff default with maxRetries=5 and base=100ms. Target SDK release 2026-03-30.

Diego Alvarez: One more thought: add a short-lived emergency token stash feature in the model-registry service that can be toggled by on-call to survive provider flaps for ~5 minutes. Low-effort mitigation while other items land. Anyone want to own the stash?

Ruth Baxter: I can add the emergency stash to the runbook and own the feature flag policy, but engineering needs to implement the stash.

Ethan Zhou: I'll add the stash to the token-broker prototype as a toggle. ETA for stash POC 2026-04-01.

Maya Singh: Great. Risks: legal/procurement may push back on SLA demands; token-broker increases blast radius; TTL increase risks expired tokens - add safety checks. Please list these in the PM under "blockers".

Priya Menon: Risk note: for TTL increase, we must validate token introspection against provider before extending TTL in prod. Will add an automated introspect step during rollout.

Diego Alvarez: Ops alert thresholds proposal: page on severity-2 if synthetic failure > 3 in 10m across any region; severity-1 if provider 5xx rate > 7% for 2m. Also add a dedicated dashboard for token-issuance latency P50/P95.

ops-bot: Created Jira tasks: RWD-9020 (token-broker-prototype) -> Ethan Zhou; RWD-9021 (cache-ttl-prefetch) -> Priya Menon; RWD-9022 (synthetic-token-checks) -> Diego Alvarez; RWD-9023 (runbook-readonly-fallback) -> Ruth Baxter; RWD-9024 (emergency-token-stash) -> Ethan Zhou. Links: https://jira.rwd/browse/RWD-9020 .../9024

Maya Singh: Please add exact ETAs and short risk bullets to the PM doc by EOD. Scheduling a 15m sync Fri 09:00 to confirm PRs and canary windows. If any owner cannot hit ETA, post here before EOD so we can reassign. :calendar:

Ethan Zhou: noted. Risk: if procurement stalls SLA, token-broker becomes higher priority.

Priya Menon: noted. Possible blocker: token introspection API has rate limits too; I'll coordinate with Diego to ensure synthetic doesn't exacerbate it.

Diego Alvarez: FYI I'm starting a 6-month pattern-scan on auth 4xx/5xx spikes and will post results next week. If we see recurrence, recommend resilience retro with platform + product to decide whether multi-provider is necessary.

Ruth Baxter: I'll version the runbook and add a recurrence-detection checklist pointing to Diego's scan ticket.

Maya Singh: Thanks all 1. Closing: update the PM doc with owner + ETA + blockers. Ops will create the epic and link tasks. ops-bot please create epic RWD-9050 for this remediation cluster.

ops-bot: Epic created: RWD-9050 (token-resilience-remediation) links RWD-9020..9024. Notifying owners and #incidents lead.
